title: Invariance moments under equality in distribution
statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be real-valued random variables on measurable spaces $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,
u)$, where $
u$ is a probability measure. If $X$ satisfies the invariance moment conditions and $X$ and $Y$ have the same distribution under $\mu$ and $
u$, then $Y$ satisfies the invariance moment conditions under $
u$.
hypotheses_covered: $X$ satisfies the invariance moment conditions under $\mu$
$X$ and $Y$ have the same distribution under $\mu$ and $\nu$
replaced: Let $X$ and $Y$ be real random variables on measured spaces $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$, where $\nu$ is a probability measure. If $X$ satisfies the invariance moment conditions and $X$ and $Y$ have the same distribution, then $Y$ is measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment and moments $\mathbb EY=\mathbb EY^3=0$, $\mathbb EY^2=1$, and $\mathbb EY^4\le9$; thus $Y$ satisfies the same moment conditions.
